criteria.criterion: OUTCOME CHANNEL. A final answer exists and is well formed: re-derived from this run's OWN trajectory by probe re-execution (the authored solver is reconstructed with its edits replayed in order, its hardcoded paths are rewritten into a sandbox over the shipped inputs, and it is executed; a literal answer-file write is the fallback), it parses, and it carries every graded case as a finite number under the task's declared output contract.

criteria.criterion: OUTCOME CHANNEL, GATE. Every graded case of the re-derived answer lands inside the task's own tolerance against the frozen truth. The answer is re-derived from this run's own trajectory by probe re-execution, never read from a reward file, so the instrument is standalone.

criteria.criterion: Opened the shipped inputs - the waveform, the station metadata or the question file - rather than working only from the prose task statement.
Authored solver source - a python file, a heredoc, or an inline `python -c` program.
Executed python to compute the magnitude.
Restricted the amplitude measurement to horizontal components, by a component-code test, by naming horizontal channel codes, or by any equivalent selection.
Deconvolved the full instrument response from the station metadata AND requested displacement output, rather than velocity, acceleration or a bare scalar sensitivity.

Simulated a Wood-Anderson torsion seismograph on the response-removed traces - a simulation call carrying the Wood-Anderson instrument, identified by name, by the conventional paz identifier, by its static magnification, or by the conjugate pole pair encoding a 0.8 s free period and 0.7 damping.
Took a peak absolute amplitude from the simulated trace and converted it from metres to millimetres before it entered the magnitude relation.
Applied the Southern-California -logA0 distance correction carrying its region-specific LOGARITHMIC distance term, not a bare 100-km reference constant or a generic attenuation curve.
Formed the magnitude as the base-10 logarithm of the amplitude plus the distance correction.
Emitted the contracted results file at the contracted path, carrying the single contracted key.

CONDITIONAL, and the condition is part of what is graded: IF the run wrote its own Wood-Anderson poles-and-zeros description, that description carries TWO zeros at the origin, as the instrument's displacement response requires. A run that simulated the Wood-Anderson from a library constant never spelled out a paz to get wrong and satisfies this criterion VACUOUSLY - it is not evidence that the run understood the zero structure, and must not be read as such.

The horizontal traces were detrended (or demeaned) and tapered before any frequency-domain operation. Any spelling of either operation counts, including obspy's detrend/taper, a manual polynomial removal, or a window applied by hand.
GUARDRAIL - the run reported a catalogue magnitude as its answer instead of measuring one from the record.
GUARDRAIL - a peak-to-peak swing was used as the amplitude without being halved to a zero-to-peak value.
GUARDRAIL - the run wrote into, deleted from, or edited in place the shipped input directory.
GUARDRAIL - the run attempted a network fetch or a package install.

The run established WHY a Wood-Anderson simulation is required - that the local magnitude scale is defined on the amplitude that instrument would have written, so the response-removed ground displacement is not the quantity the scale takes - rather than applying the simulation as an unexplained step or omitting it. Equivalent routes count: deriving it from the definition of ML, from the instrument's role in the -logA0 calibration, or from a units argument about what the amplitude term means, are all satisfactory provided the run shows why the simulation is load-bearing rather than cosmetic.

The run checked its magnitude against something that could actually have disagreed - the second horizontal component, the same chain on the other band code, the alternative distance convention with the size of the shift quoted, or an order-of-magnitude check on the simulated amplitude itself. Re-running the same script and getting the same number does not count, and neither does 'the value looks plausible' or agreement with the catalogue magnitude.

The run said which convention it was adopting at each branch that has one - displacement versus velocity output, millimetres versus metres, zero-to-peak versus peak-to-peak, which distance it fed the correction - rather than only emitting code.
